transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Um, yeah—so I’m a designer, and lately I keep getting stuck on these thoughts that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that maybe I sent the wrong version to a client. And it’s annoying because I can look at it and think, okay, this is probably fine, but then my mind just keeps circling back to it.

It’s not like some huge dramatic thing, I guess, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in. I mean, in design there really are a million little details—fonts, spacing, exports—and clients can be picky, so part of me keeps saying maybe I’m just being thorough. But it doesn’t feel like just being thorough anymore.
When these thoughts come up about possible mistakes, how do they make you feel emotionally? Do they cause you a lot of anxiety or distress?

Yeah, it does make me anxious, though I keep telling myself it shouldn’t. Like, it’s just a layout, right? And I’ve been doing design long enough that I know what a real problem looks like. But I’ll get this nagging thought that I missed some tiny mistake or sent the wrong file, and even when I can see it’s probably fine, my mind just loops back to it.

It’s not constant panic or anything, but it’s uncomfortable. Kind of like that feeling when you leave the house and wonder if you left the stove on—except it’s about kerning or export settings, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud.

When you get these thoughts about possible mistakes, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking the work over and over, re-sending files, or going through your process again—to make sure everything is perfect or to ease your mind?

Yeah… I do, unfortunately. Before I submit something now, I’ll re-open the file and sort of compare the layers, check that the right elements are there, re-save it—even if I’m pretty sure I already did. Sometimes I’ll mentally walk through every design choice again, like “why did I set it up this way, is that spacing intentional,” that kind of thing.

It doesn’t eat up my whole day or anything, and honestly designers do check things, you know? Like in school they drilled into us to look at details, and I had this one professor who would notice if something was off by a pixel, which I still think about sometimes. But now it’s more like I can’t just finish and move on as easily. It makes me slower, and I feel less free creatively, if that makes sense.
Do these thoughts and the need to check your work ever get in the way of meeting deadlines, affect your performance, or cause you significant frustration to the point it impacts your day?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting the work done, so it’s not like everything is falling apart. Clients still get their projects. But I’ve noticed I’m missing some internal deadlines more, like the little checkpoints we set before the actual due date.

And, um… this is the part that bothers me more, maybe. I think I’ve been playing it safer creatively. Like I’ll have an idea that’s more bold or more interesting, and then I start thinking, “What if there’s some detail I don’t catch, what if it makes me look careless?” So I pull back.

Which is frustrating because I’ve been wanting to move more toward a creative director role, and that’s not really the energy you want to bring into it, you know? You’re supposed to be confident with decisions, not sitting there re-checking export names like they’re going to determine your whole career.
When you go back and check your work, is it mainly to make sure everything is perfect, or is it more about trying to quiet that anxious feeling in your mind?

It’s probably more about quieting the feeling, honestly. I mean, I tell myself it’s about making sure everything is perfect, and in design there’s always another tiny thing you can adjust—layers, spacing, file names, all of that.

But the pattern is that before I submit something, I’ll re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes run through the design choices in my head one more time. And I don’t think it’s because I’m finding huge problems. It’s more like I’m trying to get my brain to let go.

It doesn’t take over my whole day, exactly, but it slows me down. And it makes me feel less free creatively, because instead of moving on, I’m sort of circling the same thing.

When you go back to check your work, does it feel like you have to do it in a specific way or a certain number of times to feel that sense of completion or relief, or is it more of a general effort to reduce worry?

It’s not really a number thing, like I don’t have to do it exactly three times or in a particular order… at least I don’t think so. It’s more that I feel unsettled until I’ve done the “usual” check.

So I’ll re-open the file, look at the layers, compare things, re-save it, and then sometimes kind of replay the design choices in my head—like, “Okay, that spacing makes sense, that element is supposed to be there.” It’s funny, because I used to be the person who could finish something and just send it, and now I feel like I need that little loop before I can let it go.

It doesn’t take over my whole day or anything, but it definitely slows me down. And creatively it makes me feel a bit boxed in, like I’m spending more energy making sure nothing is wrong than just trusting the work.
Are these thoughts about making a mistake in your work something you actively try to suppress or push away, or do they feel more like normal worries that just happen to come up often?

I guess they feel like worries at first, like normal work worries, because, I mean, mistakes do happen in design and clients can be particular. But then it keeps going past the point where it’s useful.

Like I’ll think, “Did I miss some tiny mistake in that layout?” or “What if I sent the wrong version?” And even when I can look at it and know it’s probably fine, my mind circles back to it anyway.

I don’t know if I’m actively suppressing it exactly. I try to tell myself, “You checked it, it’s okay,” and move on, but then I’ll be making coffee or looking at something else and it pops back in. It’s annoying more than anything. Like a little mental tab that won’t close.
Do the thoughts about mistakes ever feel intrusive or unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you're not actively working or thinking about a project?

Yes, they do. Not constantly, but they’ll pop up when I’m not really working anymore—like after I’ve already sent something, or I’m doing something totally unrelated.

It’ll be this nagging thought like, “What if I missed some tiny mistake in the layout?” or “What if that was the wrong version I sent?” And then I can sort of picture the file in my head, which is ridiculous because I’m not even at my computer sometimes. I might be making dinner or walking somewhere, and suddenly I’m mentally zooming in on a corner of a design.

And the frustrating thing is, I usually know it’s probably fine. Like, logically I can say, “You checked it.” But my mind still circles back to it anyway. It’s unwanted, yeah. I don’t sit there trying to think about work more—I’d actually love not to.
Have these thoughts and the need to check your work ever caused problems in your relationships, at work beyond the delays you mentioned, or in other important areas of your life?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting the work done, so it’s not like everything is falling apart. But it has started to affect things more than I’d like to admit.

I’ve missed a few internal deadlines—not client ones, mostly the team timelines where I should hand something over and I end up holding onto it because I want to check it one more time. And then one more time turns into… you know, I’ll just adjust this, I’ll just compare that version. It’s embarrassing because I used to be really quick with that stuff.

And I think it’s affecting the kind of work I put forward, too. Like, I’ll have a bolder idea, something a little more creative, and then I sort of talk myself out of it because I’m worried there’ll be some detail I missed or something that makes me look careless. Which is frustrating, because I’ve been trying to move toward more of a creative director path, and that’s literally the opposite of what I should be doing.

Sorry, I’m rambling. But yes, work-wise it’s causing problems beyond just taking extra time. In relationships, not so much, I don’t think—mostly it’s this career confidence thing.

When you have these thoughts about possible mistakes, do you find yourself doing anything in your mind repeatedly—like going over details, mentally reviewing your work, or trying to 'neutralize' the worry in some way?

Yeah, I do. It’s not like I have a whole ritual that eats up my entire day, but before I submit something now I’ll re-open the file, look through the layers, compare things again, re-save it… sometimes more than once.

And mentally, yes, I’ll sort of walk through every design choice again, like, “Why did I align it that way, did I check the spacing, was that the final logo?” It’s funny, because in design school they always drilled into us to be intentional about every choice, and I think that was useful then, but now it’s like my brain uses that against me a little.

It doesn’t take over my whole day, exactly, but it definitely slows me down. And it makes me feel less free creatively, because instead of just trusting the work, I’m double-checking and second-guessing everything.
